critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
This is better than r1, but it is not at the fern bar. The wide now reads as night. The sky (graded 11-12) sits below the facades. Dawn's stretch of pavement is the brightest on her side: graded about 58-63 against 41-43 farther along, measured on the graded JPEG. The road has good long wet streaks, and the one-point canyon with tram wires, AC boxes and balconies is a real place. The dawn frame is the best of the four: a clear eyeline to the bags, the street soft beyond, and no ghost reflection. Four things keep the stage amateur.

First, the dawn frame has a contact failure that any viewer will catch. Neither bag is in Dawn's hand. The right hand ends at y≈449 and the kraft bag's two handle peaks start at y≈464, about 5 cm below her fingertips. The handles are two separate sharp Λ peaks that never gather into the fist. The small bag's tissue sits about 20 px below the left hand. The hands are flat paddles; no grip curl shows.

Second, the window insert has lost its beat. The reflected face is 14 against 10-12 on the felt (graded 8-bit). That is invisible at normal viewing and will vanish on a YouTube encode. The frame is a dark product shot of two bags with a black hole in the middle and a flat grey slab over the left quarter (the display's felt side wall, lit evenly). The only glass cue, the pane joint at the right edge, reads as a soft dark band. 8.9 % of pixels are below 8/255.

Third, the signs carry the location, and they read as paint chips. Nearly every raw face sits at v150-165 and s0.5-0.6 (the yellow is s0.84), so after grade A they are pastel cards at s0.29-0.44 and v about 90-125. Lavender, mint, sky blue, pink and tan all have equal weight and are spread evenly over the upper half, with no hierarchy. Two are cut at the top edge of the frame.

Fourth, the pavement joints still glow as green, pink and violet hairlines. On the graded dawn frame about 190 violet-pink joint pixels left of Dawn have saturation above 0.3 and a channel above 60; the green dashes are fainter. They read as LED strips set in the floor, in dawn and company alike.

Smaller problems:
- The company frame reads as two bodyguards escorting her, not as hosts treating her well.
- Dawn's right calf (frame right) glows as bare stone in company: 60 against 30 on the other leg, and up to about 159 in a band just under the hem.
- A hard white triangle of light on the shop wall right of Dawn in the wide (up to 155) competes with her. It is as bright as her head and many times its area. The same light puts a pale wedge at the right edge of company.
- A teal sign reflection smears across the tote in the dawn frame.
- The shelf bags in window and dawn carry the evidence purses' colours (cognac tote, black satchel). The coverage brief rules that out, although r1 asked for the cognac. The lead should settle which holds.

No text or logo reads anywhere. Two shapes come close to glyphs. The tram at the vanishing point shows only as two stacked grey bars, an '=' exactly where the eye rests. The end building's teal panel has a far violet sign notched into its left side, so it reads as a bracket.

Per camera: wide about 6, dawn about 5.5 (it would be 6.5 without the floating bags and the floor glints), window about 4.5, company about 5. Mean about 5.2.
answers:
Your measurements first. I checked them on the published frames.
- Pavement near Dawn against farther along: graded 58-63 against 41-43 on my boxes, about 1.4-1.5x. Your 68/39 (1.7x) matches the raw (68-73 against 41-43). Either way her stretch is the brightest on that side.
- Sky against facade: the sky slot is 12 graded, below the facades beside it. The inversion is gone.
- The turquoise sign is now clear of the laundry in both wide and dawn.
- The tote: graded h28 s0.50 v0.29, raw h28 s0.92. The measurement is right and it reads as cognac, no longer khaki. But see the note on the shelf bags under 4.
- The reflected face: 14 against 10-12. Your number is right, but that number is the problem (see 4).

1. Colour and spacing of the blank signs.

Spacing: the overlap rejection works, and the r1 stepped glyph is gone. There is now a dark sign-free slot at top centre: mean 13, p98 19 over x 480-680, y 0-180, clean from about x 470 to 710 at the very top. It is the natural home for the HONG KONG super the script puts on the wide. At 200-240 px it is narrow. A Cormorant super at a comfortable size (cap height about 40-50 px) needs about 300-380 px, so widen the slot if the super goes there (fix 7).

Colour: this fails. Nearly every lightbox sits at the same raw value (v150-165, s0.5-0.6), so AgX and grade A's 0.55 saturation turn them all into equal-weight pastels: graded s0.29-0.44 at v about 90-125. The upper half reads as a swatch book of lavender, mint, sky blue, pink and tan, evenly sprinkled. The script wants a warm Hong Kong ('warm Chicago and Hong Kong; cold fluorescent from the check-in desk on'), and nothing here is warm. The nearest signs do light their walls: beside the left teal sign the wall is raw about 59 against 27 just below it. Two limits: only signs nearer than y 90 get spill lights, and at most 60 such lights. With every face equally bright, the spill builds no hierarchy.

There are also two edge cuts: the purple panel across the top edge (x 730-1075, y 0-25) and the tan panel at the top-left corner. On the right, the tan, lavender, teal and blue panels stack with offset edges (x 690-760, y 260-420), which still makes L-steps. No panel reads as a letter.

2. Where the street light draws the eye.

The two nearest street-lamp heads tie for the brightest pixel in the wide, at L 224:
- lamp_30's lens at (506, 289), inside the left sign cluster;
- lamp_64's lens at (646, 408), about 190 px left of Dawn and 100 px above her.
Both are the 'street lamp lens' emitter at strength 30. They are hard, cool-white slivers after the grade. Their pools on the road do not register visibly, so they pull the eye up and away without lighting anything.

Two other things compete around Dawn:
- The boutique's own blank fascia lightbox (x 840-925, y 372-398, peaks about 150). It is designed, and it is fine once the wedge below is gone.
- A hard-edged white triangle on the shop wall just right of her (x 950-975, y 490-540, up to 155). It sits about a metre from the 'boutique door spill' light. It is about as bright as her head (most of her head is 110-140, its peak about 170) and many times its area. It is far brighter than her bags (the kraft bag peaks about 86 in the wide).

Net: the eye goes to the signs, then to the wedge, then to Dawn. It should go street → pool → Dawn.

3. The three walkers with empty hands (company).

The empty hands read clearly, and they are what the brief asks for: COVERAGE row 9 says 'no faces, no gesture, nobody carrying anything of hers'. The problem is what the shot says. The two men are near-identical in build and charcoal (T1 0.1/0.105/0.125, the Organiser 0.1/0.1/0.11). They flank her in an evenly spaced line, about 0.7 m apart and evenly staggered in depth. Both lead with the right foot, so they walk in step. All heads face square ahead and no one turns to anyone. That reads as a custody escort, not 'the people running the trip treated her well, and every expense was covered'.

Continuity: she carries two bags in wide and dawn, and company follows dawn in Ch 03. The brief chose empty hands, so flag the jump for the edit rather than changing the stage.

Her right calf (frame right) glows as bare stone: 60 against 30 on the other leg, and a band just under the hem reaches about 159. That band is probably where the tights mask fades over the knee (the thigh.001 weights are scaled to 0.85), under the door spill at 0.62. The same light probably makes the pale wedge at the right edge of the frame (x 1195-1280, y 130-260). The pavement hairline glints run straight up the middle of the frame between the figures. The stride, grounding and contact shadows are fine.

4. Does the face read in the glass while the satchel stays clear in the three-quarter view?

The satchel stays clear in dawn. There is no ghost figure now, and the shoulder bag on the plinth is visible too. But the face does not read in window. In the graded insert the head-shaped patch (about x 620-770, y 50-250) is 14 against a 10-12 surround. You can only find it with an autocontrast stretch. On a YouTube encode, near black, it will not exist.

r1's target was 'no more than 1.25x the felt'. At these levels a ratio is meaningless: what makes a reflection visible is the absolute step. Aim for about +10 to +14 code values over the felt, with soft edges: the face at about 24-28 graded over felt at 12-14. That is still well under r1's 56-over-33 ghost. Without it, the insert loses its idea (Dawn's own image hanging over the bags) and becomes a catalogue shot. No signs show in the glass either. They are not hidden from glossy rays for this camera; the reflection floor (0.002) is simply too low to carry them.

The shelf bags: the brief in COVERAGE (rows 124 and 353, written before r1) puts the shelf bags where the three purses sit in evidence_table/purses and says none should have their colours. They now show a cognac tote and a black satchel, the same colours as the evidence tote and satchel. r1 asked for the cognac, so this is the critics' conflict, not your error. The purses are given to her later, on the mainland, so these are shop bags that only rhyme with the prize. Get the lead's ruling before changing them (fix 8).

In dawn, a teal sign reflection also lies as a green smear across the front of the cognac tote (x 940-955, y 310-335), which reads as a stain.

What each camera still lacks for its beat:
- wide: signs with hierarchy and warm colour, and the eye led to Dawn rather than to a wall wedge and two lamp heads.
- dawn: bags actually held, and no floor LEDs.
- window: a visible reflection and some evidence of glass.
- company: warmth or hosting within the brief, not an escort.

fixes.problem: Neither bag is held. The kraft bag's two handle peaks start about 5 cm below the right hand (hand ends y≈449, handles y≈464). The handles do not gather, and the small bag's tissue sits about 20 px below the left hand. The hands read as flat paddles.
fixes.fix:
Stop trusting grip_point() from hand_fk.tail in hang_bag():
1. After ground(h), evaluate Dawn's body mesh and take the vertices weighted more than 0.5 to DEF-f_middle.01.{side} and DEF-f_index.01.{side}. Use their centroid, minus 0.015 m along the palm normal, as the handle apex.
2. In bag_mesh(), give both handles the same apex (apex = Vector((0,0,0)) for both s), so the two loops meet inside the fist.
3. Make each loop a rounded quadratic and drop the 0.55·sin² pinch that makes the sharp peak.
4. Raise CURL_GRIP so a fist closes round the handles: f_index (75,85), f_middle (80,88), f_ring (80,85), f_pinky (78,80), thumb (35,40).
5. Add a check that prints the distance from each bag's apex to the nearest finger vertex. Require it to be under 0.012 m on both sides for the 'window' and 'walk' beats.
6. Re-render dawn and inspect the hands at 4x.

fixes.problem: Dawn's reflection is invisible (graded 14 against felt 10-12), so the insert loses its beat. 8.9 % of pixels are below 8/255. The only glass cue, the pane joint at the right edge, reads as a soft dark band.
fixes.fix:
Light and glass:
1. In TRIMS['window'], raise bq_glow from 0.18 to about 0.55.
2. Set CAMERAS['window'] glass_refl to 0.012 and keep glass_grazing at 0.36. Signboards are already visible to glossy rays for this camera (hide_glossy holds only shop_interiors and tubes), so the stronger reflection should bring two or three soft sign colours into the top corners without other changes.
3. In mats.shop_glass(), name the smudge map-range node and set its output range to about 0.04-0.12 for this camera from apply_camera, so the face is soft, not a sharp double exposure.

Target, measured on the graded JPEG: the face patch (about x 620-770, y 50-250) at 24-28, the felt beside it at 12-14, and the face's edge blurred over at least 6 px.

Glass cue: the d1 stile at y 19.95 is about 15 degrees outside the left frame edge, so it cannot be used. Give the existing pane joint (the bead at y 18.118-18.130, frame x about 1190-1230) a thin bevel that catches bq_top or bq_spill as a narrow highlight.

Black floor: lift it so no more than 3 % of pixels are under 8/255. Either raise the felt's base colour by about 30 % or raise CAMERAS['window'] exposure from -1.3 to about -1.15. Keep grade A as it is.

fixes.problem: The pavement joints glint as green, pink and violet hairlines: about 190 violet-pink pixels with saturation above 0.3 in the graded dawn paving (x 308-439, y 463-703), and the same up the middle of company. They read as LED strips set in the floor.
fixes.fix:
1. In mats.pavers(), drop the joint term from the bump height: h = noise(90)·(1-wet) only. The joint step tilts the slab-edge normals on the wet areas (roughness 0.03), and those normals catch the sign colours. The roughness mix with 'joint' covers only the joint itself, not that slope.
2. Add a second ShaderNodeTexBrick at the same scale with Mortar Size 0.04 and Mortar Smooth 0.6. Use (1 - its Factor) as 'band', and force roughness to at least 0.55 within about 2 cm of every joint: r = _fmix(nt, band, r, 0.6).

Check on the graded dawn and company frames: no paving pixel within 5 px of a joint has saturation above 0.25 and a channel above 60.

fixes.problem: Nearly every sign face sits at the same raw value (v150-165, s0.5-0.6), so the graded signs are equal-weight pastels (s0.29-0.44, v about 90-125): a paint-chip catalogue with no hierarchy, and nothing warm in a Hong Kong the script calls warm.
fixes.fix:
1. In signs(), replace the 'box' strength draw rng.uniform(1.0, 2.2) with a skewed mapping of the same single draw, so the street layout's random sequence does not change. Take u = rng.uniform(0, 1): u < 0.6 gives dim, 0.25-0.5; u < 0.9 gives mid, 0.6-1.0; otherwise hero, 1.4-2.0.
2. Allow hero signs only on the right side for 8 < yw < 30, and clamp them to mid elsewhere, so the brightest colour clusters around Dawn.
3. Warm the palette. SIGN_COL's warm, amber and cream are now nearly the same orange, because r1 replaced the near-whites. Add one warm-white, for example (1.0, 0.8, 0.55), and weight SIGN_W roughly: warm-white 4, amber 4, warm 2, magenta 2, teal 1.5, violet 1, blue 1, yellow 1, green 0.5, cool 0.5, cream 0.
4. Raise the sign-spill power from 8·reach·h·strength to about 14·reach·h·strength, so the dimmer signs keep the wall spill the left teal sign has now.

Check on the graded wide:
- raw faces at s 0.75 or more at v100-140, and graded s 0.40 or more;
- the spread of face values (p90 minus p10) at least 50 code values;
- walls within 1 m of a lit sign at least 1.6x the same wall 3 m away.

fixes.problem: Two things pull the eye from Dawn. A hard white triangle on the shop wall right of her (x 950-975, y 490-540, up to 155) is as bright as her head and many times its area. The two nearest street-lamp lenses tie for the frame maximum at L 224: lamp_30 at (506, 289) and lamp_64 at (646, 408).
fixes.fix:
1. The triangle is very probably the 'boutique door spill' area light. It sits at (7.15, 15.0, 1.94), 5 cm off the building line and about a metre from that wall, and its 68-degree spread cuts a hard edge across the wall. Confirm by rendering wide with that light at 0.
2. Then light-link it to a collection of Dawn's meshes, the two shopping bags and street_ground, the way 'boutique pavement spill' is already linked. That keeps its warm light on her shoulder, the handles and the paving, and it should also clear the matching pale wedge at the right edge of company (x 1195-1280, y 130-260).
3. In mats, drop M['lamp_head'] ('street lamp lens') emission from 30 to about 12, so the lamp heads are no longer the frame maximum.

Check on the graded wide: nothing within 150 px of Dawn larger and brighter than her head, and both lamp heads under 170.

fixes.problem: The shot reads as a custody escort: two near-identical dark-suited men flank Dawn in step (both lead with the right foot) in an evenly spaced line, all heads square ahead. Her right calf (frame right) glows as bare stone: 60 against 30, with a band just under the hem up to about 159.
fixes.fix:
Keep everyone's hands empty. COVERAGE row 9 asks for 'no faces, no gesture, nobody carrying anything of hers', so do not give her bag to the Organiser. Make it read as company within that brief:
1. Take the men out of step: give T1 lead L, or a clearly different stride length.
2. Break the even line: move T1 about 0.4 m back (y about 15.7), and let the Organiser walk a little closer to Dawn (x about 6.25).
3. Turn the Organiser's head 10-15 degrees toward her: solve_head with her eye_centre as target, clamped so no face shows from behind. Turn Dawn's head 5-10 degrees toward him.
4. Tell the men apart: keep T1's male_casualsuit05 but retint it to a lighter, still muted brown-grey such as (0.2, 0.18, 0.15), and keep the Organiser charcoal.

Leg:
1. Raise the DEF-thigh.L.001 and DEF-thigh.R.001 scales in tights() from 0.85 to 1.0, so the tights cover the knee.
2. Trim 'boutique door spill' for company from 0.62 to about 0.35.
3. If needed, lower tights() value from 0.07 to about 0.05.
Target: the lit calf and knee at or under 1.3x the shaded leg.

Leave the dawn-to-company bag continuity to the lead for the edit.

fixes.problem: The dark slot for the HONG KONG super is only about 200-240 px wide (clean from about x 470 to 710 at the top). Two signs are cut by the top edge: the purple panel at x 730-1075, y 0-25, and the tan panel at the top-left corner.
fixes.fix:
If the super goes at top centre, add two rules to separated_sign(), which works in tangent units (-p.x/p.z, -p.y/p.z) of the wide camera. For lens 24 on a 36 mm sensor with shift_y 0.12, the frame spans x ±0.75 and y from about -0.24 at the bottom to +0.60 at the top. Pixel x maps to (x-640)/640·0.75; pixel y maps to 0.602 - y/720·0.844.
1. Reject any sign whose rectangle overlaps the box x 450-830, y 0-190 px: x1 > -0.223, x0 < 0.223 and y1 > 0.379. This removes the lavender panel at x 712-790 and the top purple one, so check that the right cluster still reads full.
2. Reject any sign that crosses or comes within 12 px of the top edge: y1 > 0.588 while y0 < 0.602. Signs cut by the left or right edges are normal in a canyon; leave those.

A rejection in separated_sign already leaves the random sequence unchanged, because every draw comes before it.

Target: graded p98 at or below 25 over x 450-830, y 0-190.

fixes.problem: A teal sign reflection lies as a green smear across the cognac tote (x 940-955, y 310-335), so the shelf bag looks stained. The kraft bag is a flat beige card (graded s0.17, v0.49), the brightest object after her head.
fixes.fix:
Smear: remove the reflection over the shelf band for this camera only. Window needs the same glass to carry Dawn's face, so the change must be per camera:
- either add an Object-Z mask to the shop_glass mix that takes the reflection to 0 between z 0.9 and 1.5 m, switched on from apply_camera only for 'dawn';
- or trim the reflection floor for dawn.
Setting signboards visible_glossy=False for dawn would also delete the signs' streaks on the wet road at the left of this frame, so avoid it.

Kraft bag and tissue:
1. Trim 'display shelf return' for dawn from 28 W to about 12 W. It is linked only to the shopping bags and Dawn's suit.
2. Raise the kraft crumple bump from 0.12 to about 0.3 and add three or four creases (a Voronoi distance-to-edge term at scale 6), so the bag reads as paper at v about 0.33.
3. Replace the five tissue cones with three crumpled planes (a subdivided grid displaced by noise, about 0.03 m), so the tissue reads as paper, not white plastic spikes.

fixes.problem: The shelf bags show a cognac tote and a black satchel, the colours of the tote and satchel in evidence_table/purses. COVERAGE (rows 124 and 353) asks that none has their colours, although r1 asked for the cognac. The same bags show in dawn and company.
fixes.fix: Do not change this until the lead rules. If the coverage brief holds, recolour the boutique bags through the hue, sat and val settings in boutique()'s spec so that none reads as cognac, black or burgundy, keeping their places. If r1's cognac holds, record that in the brief.

fixes.problem: At the vanishing point the tram shows only as two stacked grey bars, an '=' where the eye rests. The end building's teal panel (x 591-600, y 472-498) has a far violet sign notched into its left side, so it reads as a bracket.
fixes.fix:
Tram:
1. In tram(), give the body a painted material, dark green (0.05, 0.09, 0.07) at roughness 0.5, instead of G['railing'], so it reads against the haze.
2. Split each end window band into three panes with 6 cm mullions.
3. Add two small warm headlights at z 0.9, strength about 8, and one plain blank route box on the roof.

Near-glyph: col2 and field are already ignored in sign_box(), and separated_sign() already runs at every depth. The bracket happens because end_building() runs after the street's signs and its four panels are never added to _BASE['sign_rectangles'], so no street sign is tested against them. Register the end-building panels' projected rectangles before the buildings are built, and reject any sign that overlaps one.

fixes.problem: The left quarter is a flat grey slab (graded about 25, featureless): the display's felt side wall at y 20.01, lit evenly by the spots. At the top right, the upper shelf's small blank block reads as another grey slab.
fixes.fix:
1. Swing the window camera's aim 2-3 degrees right (toward -y), so less of the side wall shows. Keep the tote's left handle clear of the frame edge; the pane joint stays in frame.
2. Keep the felt, which is the designed display box, but give the side wall a falloff instead of an even wash, darkening it toward the glass. Either exclude it from bq_top by light linking, or let it fall off naturally.
3. On the upper shelf, give the existing block (the dress box at x 8.11-8.39, y 18.28-18.54) an edge or lid line and a little more light, so it reads as an object, such as a blank scarf box, not a slab.
